name: Kurdish (Kurmanji)
notes: Northern Kurdish / Kurmanji (kurdî, Kurmancî), the largest Kurdish variety. The mapping above is the 31-letter Hawar Latin alphabet (Celadet Alî Bedirxan, 1932), the script of the ku Wikipedia and of Kurmanji in Turkey, Syria and the diaspora. The Kurdo-Arabic (Sorani-style) alphabet and the former Soviet Cyrillic alphabet are also used for Kurdish and are NOT modelled here — Hawar Latin input is assumed. Aspiration of /p t k/ is contrastive but unwritten.

sources.author: Thackston, W. M.
sources.title: Kurmanji Kurdish: A Reference Grammar with Selected Readings
sources.publisher: Harvard University, Iranian Studies (distributed free by the author; archived copy)
sources.notes: 'Alphabet and sounds' (pp. 1-3), read in full. Confirms the Hawar Latin letter set and ⟨c⟩ = dʒ, ⟨ç⟩ = tʃ, ⟨j⟩ = ʒ, ⟨ş⟩ = ʃ, ⟨x⟩ = x, ⟨q⟩ = q, ⟨w y⟩ = w j. Four vowel values differ from this map: ⟨e⟩ is æ as the standard reading (ɛ for many speakers, and before ⟨y⟩ or post-stress), ⟨a⟩ is ɑ, ⟨u⟩ is ʊ (ɪ-like or ʉ only in gu/ku), and Thackston states no length contrast, so the map's aː eː iː for ⟨a ê î⟩ are not his. He also records what the spelling does not show: ⟨p t k ç⟩ each stand for an aspirated and an unaspirated pharyngealised consonant, and ⟨h⟩ covers both h and the pharyngeal ħ in the areas that have it. Recorded here, not changed.
